topic: Email: feedback request after a hotel stay
context: Dear Guest, thank you for choosing Riverside Hotel for your recent stay. We hope you enjoyed your time with us, and we are writing to ask for a few minutes of your time to share your experience. Your feedback helps us improve the service for future guests, and we read every response carefully. Could you please rate the following: the warmth of our welcome at check-in, the comfort of your room, the quality of the breakfast buffet, and the helpfulness of our staff during your stay? You can complete the short form on our website, and it will take no more than five minutes. If anything fell short of your expectations, please tell us in the form so that we can address it directly. As a thank-you, every completed survey will receive a voucher for fifteen percent off your next booking. We value your opinion and hope to welcome you back again soon.

items.prompt: Why is the hotel asking for feedback?
items.key: To improve the transport for future guests.
d: To meet a requirement from management.
To fill in an annual survey requirement.

topic: News report: local farmers switch to organic growing
context: A growing number of farmers in the northern region are switching to organic growing methods, and the results so far are encouraging. According to the regional agriculture office, more than three hundred farms have stopped using chemical pesticides and fertilizers in favor of compost, crop rotation, and natural pest control. Farmers report that although yields took a year or two to stabilize, the soil has become healthier and water use has fallen. Consumers, meanwhile, have shown a strong preference for organic produce, with supermarket chains expanding their organic sections to meet demand. The agriculture office has launched a training program to help farmers transition smoothly, offering workshops on soil management and natural pest control. Officials caution that organic farming requires more labor and careful planning, but say the long-term benefits for soil health and farm income make the switch worthwhile.

items.prompt: What have the farmers stopped using?
items.key: Chemical pesticides and fertilizers.

context: The Metropolitan Transit Authority wishes to inform all passengers of a fare adjustment that will take effect from the first of next month. The basic single-trip fare will increase from twenty baht to twenty-five baht, while monthly passes will remain unchanged at one thousand baht. The adjustment is necessary, the authority explains, because fuel and maintenance costs have risen sharply over the past two years, and the previous fares did not cover these increases. Students, senior citizens, and holders of disabled cards will continue to receive a fifty percent discount on all trips. The authority has also promised to add twenty more buses on the busiest routes during peak hours to improve service as part of the same package. Passengers are encouraged to use the monthly pass for unlimited travel and to check the new fare tables at stations and on the authority's website.

items.prompt: What will the new basic single-trip fare be?
items.key: Twenty-five baht.
items.exp: ประกาศระบุ “The basic single-trip fare will increase from twenty baht to twenty-five baht” จึงตอบ 25 บาท ตัวเลือก 20/30/15/ฟรี ขัดกับประกาศ

items.prompt: Why is the fare being adjusted?

items.exp: ประกาศระบุ “because fuel and maintenance costs have risen sharply” จึงตอบค่าน้ำมันและบำรุงรักษาเพิ่มขึ้น ตัวเลือกซื้อรถใหม่/ผู้โดยสารลด/ปรับปรุงสถานี/ monthly pass ถูก ไม่มีข้อมูล

items.prompt: In the passage, what does “these increases” refer to?

d: The increases in monthly pass prices.

items.exp: ข้อความ “the previous fares did not cover these increases” อ้างถึงค่าน้ำมันและค่าบำรุงรักษาที่สูงขึ้น ตัวเลือกผู้โดยสาร/ monthly pass/ เส้นทาง/ ส่วนลด ไม่ใช่สิ่งถูกอ้างถึง

topic: Article: how libraries are adapting to digital readers
context: Libraries are no longer just places to borrow printed books. Across the country, public libraries are rethinking their role to serve readers who increasingly choose digital formats. Many have expanded their e-book collections, allowing readers to borrow titles on phones and tablets without visiting the building. Others have created comfortable spaces with charging points and quiet zones for people who want to read or study on their own devices. Library managers say the change is not about replacing print, but about meeting readers where they are. Visits to the children's reading hours remain strong, and printed picture books remain popular with young families. The challenge, staff say, is keeping the physical spaces welcoming while managing the growing demand for digital access and public computers. The future library, they argue, will offer both — a place to gather and a gateway to digital reading.

items.prompt: What have many libraries expanded to serve digital readers?
items.key: Their e-book collections.

items.prompt: What do library managers say the change is not about?

context: Love taking photos? Join our two-day weekend photography workshop, designed for beginners who want to get more from their camera or phone. On day one, you will learn the basics: how light works, how to frame a shot, and how to choose the right setting for different situations. Day two is a practical outdoor session at the old town, where you will practice capturing portraits, street scenes, and architecture with guidance from a professional photographer. All equipment is provided, so you don't need to own a camera — just bring your phone or borrow one of ours. The workshop runs from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on both days, with a lunch break and a short review of each participant's photos at the end. The fee is 2,400 baht, which includes all materials, lunch, and a printed guide to keep. Spaces are limited to twelve participants, so book early to avoid missing out.
